entries.name: Kiroween 2026 (Kiro by AWS, Devpost hackathon)
entries.agency: Kiro (agentic AI IDE from Amazon Web Services), managed by Devpost
entries.amount: $100,000 in cash prizes (Devpost page: "Expect $100,000 in cash prizes"; prize split "Prizes TBD" until rules post on Oct 30, 2026)
entries.close_quote: You will have until Friday, December 4, 2026 at 2:00 PM Pacific Time to build and submit your project.
entries.eligibility: Devpost listing: "Above legal age of majority in country of residence"; "All countries/territories, excluding standard exceptions". Needs a valid Kiro user ID or AWS account ID to register. Only new projects built during the Oct 30 - Dec 4 submission period are eligible.
entries.note: OFFICIAL RULES NOT YET POSTED (released Oct 30, 2026), SO WHETHER COMPANIES CAN ENTER AND HOW PRIZES ARE SPLIT ARE NOT YET CONFIRMED. DO NOT START BUILDING BEFORE OCT 30 (pre-built work is ineligible). Not health-specific: theme categories are Resurrection, Frankenstein, Skeleton Crew and Costume Contest. Registration is open now; Vybe can register Monday and build an open DevKit/SDK starter template (Skeleton Crew) or a band-data app with Kiro once submissions open. Online, free.
documents: Kiro user ID or AWS account ID
New project built with Kiro during Oct 30 - Dec 4, 2026
Submission per rules to be posted Oct 30 (typically repo, demo video, description)
entries.fit_why: Vybe enters as a developer team building a Kiro-made SDK starter template or wearable-data app (Skeleton Crew / Frankenstein categories); the contest is general-purpose, not health, and the rules that post on Oct 30 could restrict entrant type.
entries.big_name_why: Kiro is Amazon Web Services' agentic IDE (kiro.dev lists AWS as parent organization), so a win is an AWS-branded developer prize with real cash and visibility in the AWS developer community.
entries.evidence: Kiroween 2026 Oct 30 – Dec 4, 2026 ... Expect $100,000 in cash prizes. ... You will need a valid Kiro user ID or AWS account ID to register.

entries.name: Kiro for Startups: up to one year of free Kiro Pro+ credits (AWS)
entries.amount: "up to one year's worth of Kiro Pro+ credits" in three tiers: Starter (up to 2 Kiro users), Growth (up to 10), Scale (up to 30); dollar value not stated on the page (checked 2026-10-17)
entries.close_quote: From April 7, 2026 to December 31, 2026, apply at https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/kiro to receive complimentary access to Kiro Pro+, and one year of Kiro Promotion Credits
entries.eligibility: Early stage to Series A startups; official business email matching the startup's domain; AWS Account ID created with that matching email; applicant 18+; not resident in the excluded countries (US is not excluded). Startups with active AWS Activate credits are not eligible.
entries.note: STARTUPS WITH ACTIVE AWS ACTIVATE CREDITS ARE NOT ELIGIBLE: AWS Activate is already on the board, so pick one path; if Vybe already holds Activate credits, skip this (Activate credits can be spent on Kiro instead). Credits expire one year after issuance and overage billing to the AWS card follows. Requires a domain-matched business email. Reviewed on a rolling basis; window ends Dec 31, 2026.
documents: AWS account with domain-matched business email
entries.fit_why: Vybe enters as an early-stage startup building firmware, SDK and API code with an AI IDE; it is disqualified if it already holds active AWS Activate credits.
entries.big_name_why: An AWS-issued credit for Amazon's own AI IDE, credited straight to Vybe's AWS account; it is a credential with AWS's startup team more than a public win.
entries.evidence: For a limited time only, early stage to Series A startups globally can apply for up to 1-year's worth of free Kiro Pro+ at three-tiered options. Startups with active AWS Activate Credits are not eligible for this promotion

entries.name: University of Cincinnati 1819 Innovation Hub: UC Venture Lab Accelerator (rolling intake for the next fall/spring cohort)
entries.agency: University of Cincinnati, 1819 Innovation Hub (Venture Lab)
entries.amount: Nondilutive grant capital purpose-built for technology and commercial validation ... The Venture Lab deploys up to $1 million per year in funding designed to fund the specific milestones that move a company up the technology readiness level (TRL) scale.
entries.close_quote: The Venture Lab Accelerator runs twice a year, in the fall and spring ... (application form: "The form takes about 5 minutes and we'll follow up with the right next step for you.")
entries.eligibility: Any entrepreneur or startup (UC affiliation not required; the accelerator is free to community members). Ventures in hard tech, deep tech or health tech with a working MVP or prototype, a validated market, a committed team, and a clear path to building, hiring and scaling in Ohio.
entries.note: NEEDS A WORKING MVP OR PROTOTYPE (NOT JUST A CONCEPT); 10-WEEK RESIDENCY AT THE 1819 HUB IN CINCINNATI; PAGE STRESSES GROWTH IN CINCINNATI AND SOUTHWEST OHIO, BUT THE STATED CRITERION IS 'POTENTIAL TO GROW IN OHIO', WHICH AKRON MEETS. The per-company grant size is not stated; $1M a year is the programme's total. No cohort deadline is posted: the Airtable form is open now and the team follows up. Selective: 7 to 8 ventures per cohort. The fall 2026 cohort includes an IoT sensor platform (NetNeural) and a health app (Rellax), which shows hardware/health fit.
documents: Venture Lab Accelerator Airtable application (about 5 minutes): https://airtable.com/appOIe1TaqsIbEctP/shrW5hCxhFIOzmFOe
Evidence of a working MVP or prototype (DevKit / band)
entries.fit_why: Vybe comes in as an Ohio health-tech/hard-tech hardware startup (band plus SDK) seeking nondilutive milestone grants. It is disqualified if the DevKit is not yet a working prototype, or if founders cannot commit to the 10-week Cincinnati residency.
entries.big_name_why: The University of Cincinnati is an Ohio flagship research university, and its 1819 Innovation Hub is a major Ohio innovation centre. Getting in brings UC grant money plus Fortune 500 entrepreneurs-in-residence, the UC tech-transfer office and corporate partner introductions.
entries.evidence: "In the Venture Lab Accelerator, which is free to community members, entrepreneurs in residence from Fortune 500 companies can help to vet your startup idea" / "Do I need to be a UC student or faculty member to start a company through the 1819 Hub? No." / "Nondilutive funding is available alongside the program"

entries.name: Henry Ford Health + Michigan State University Innovation Hub: startup collaboration intake (pilot sites, customer discovery, entrepreneurial support)
entries.agency: Henry Ford Health + Michigan State University (Innovation Hub, with the MSU Research Foundation)
entries.amount: amount not stated on the page (checked 2026-10-17)
entries.close_quote: We accept applications on a rolling basis. To be considered, please complete the Innovation Hub Intake Form. (Innovation Fund page; the intake form is live, Microsoft Forms status Active)
entries.eligibility: Health care startups seeking collaboration with Henry Ford Health / MSU. The intake form asks for country, state and location, so out-of-state companies can apply. It is not for product sales, service promotions or vendor solicitations.
entries.note: NOT CASH: THE INTAKE OPENS COLLABORATION (PILOT SITES, CUSTOMER DISCOVERY, MENTORING, IP CO-DEVELOPMENT). THE FORM ASKS 'HOW DO YOU PLAN TO FUND YOUR COLLABORATION WITH HENRY FORD HEALTH?', SO A PILOT MAY BE AT VYBE'S COST. THE ATTACHED INNOVATION FUND IS EQUITY (SAFEs/notes/preferred) AND NEEDS A DELAWARE OR MICHIGAN C-CORP; IT IS LISTED SEPARATELY UNDER REJECTED. 'Clinical pilot studies' is one option among several, not a requirement. Pitch it as a wellness/research DevKit pilot, never a diagnostic. Similar health-system intakes already on the board: UH Partner and OhioHealth NVBI.
documents: Innovation Hub Intake Form (Microsoft Forms): company name, website, location/state/country, date founded, product summary, type of product, development stage, traction and validation, differentiation, value/ROI pathway, goals with Henry Ford, how the collaboration will be funded, dilutive and non-dilutive capital raised, revenue YTD/TTM, funding stage, next financing round
entries.fit_why: Vybe would enter as a DevKit design-partner/pilot candidate, giving Henry Ford's clinical and research teams a research-grade wearable. It is disqualified if Henry Ford wants a paid vendor pilot or a clinical-validation study that Vybe cannot staff.
entries.big_name_why: Henry Ford Health is a nationally known Detroit health system, and Michigan State is a Big Ten flagship. A yes opens supervised clinical pilot sites, reference customers and a strategic investor arm.
entries.evidence: "Complete this form to explore collaboration with the shared excellence of our partnership, including but not limited to entrepreneurial support, customer discovery, venture investment, co-development of intellectual property and clinical pilot studies." / "We offer supervised access to those clinical settings for you to test, iterate, and validate products with health care providers."

entries.name: HHS OASH KidneyX Prize: Nourishing Kidney Health (FY27), Track 2 Nutrition & Lifestyle
entries.agency: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health (InnovationX), with the American Society of Nephrology (KidneyX public-private partnership)
entries.amount: Total Cash Prizes $4,670,000 ... Track 2 KidneyX Innovator Prize of $335,000 (Up to 4 Potential Prizes); Track 2 KidneyX Grand Prize of $1,000,000
entries.close_quote: Submission period begins: May , 3 2027 05:00 PM EST Submission period ends: July 23, 2027, 5:00 PM ET
entries.eligibility: Individuals, teams or entities; a private entity 'shall be incorporated in and maintain a primary place of business in the United States'; 18+; not a federal entity. Open to 'startups, community organizations, food-system innovators, and technology developers'. Entry is a signed HHS registration form plus a submission, both emailed to kidneyXprize@hhs.gov. SAM/UEI is 'encouraged, but not required'.
entries.note: KIDNEY-ANCHORED (CKD PREVENTION VIA CARDIO-KIDNEY-METABOLIC SYNDROME): THIS IS CLOSE TO THE SINGLE-DISEASE RULE. It is listed only because Track 2 is a whole-person lifestyle track ('physical activity, metabolic health, sleep, stress') and federal prizes like NIH NOURISH are already on the board. SUBMISSIONS 'MUST DEMONSTRATE FEASIBILITY OR PRELIMINARY EFFECTIVENESS' WITH EMPIRICAL EVIDENCE, AND MUST 'MEANINGFULLY ENGAGE PEOPLE LIVING WITH KIDNEY DISEASE'. Vybe has no such data today. It needs a DevKit pilot with a nephrology clinic, a community health partner or a university by mid-2027. Avoid Track 1, which centres on CKM risk identification and comes close to a diagnostic claim. The window is confirmed but not open until 3 May 2027 (the page's own typo reads 'May , 3 2027'). The rules were revised on 21 Sep 2026. The prize is a cash prize, not a grant: 'HHS does not limit how winners may use prize money awarded to them.' The board's kind list has no prize value, so 'grant' is the nearest fit.
documents: Signed HHS Challenge Participant Registration Form (PDF, register as an entity)
Whole-person lifestyle support: activity, sleep, stress (100 words)
Measurement and learning: outcome measures (100 words)
Track 2 evidence of feasibility or preliminary effectiveness plus implementation and scaling plan (150 words)
entries.fit_why: Vybe can enter Track 2 with a screenless band that turns sleep, HRV and activity into lifestyle feedback inside a partner's kidney-protective nutrition and coaching programme. It fails if Vybe has no pilot evidence or kidney-patient engagement by July 2027.
entries.big_name_why: A federal HHS prize under the America COMPETES Act, run with the American Society of Nephrology: a win is a federal award that carries weight with health systems and payers.
entries.evidence: Solutions may address personalized CKM risk identification, care and/or nutrition, Food Is Medicine, behavioral incentives, digital coaching, physical activity, food access, and underserved populations. ... Entities participating in this Challenge are encouraged, but not required, to request and obtain a free Unique Entity ID (UEI) ... via SAM.gov
